title: Include source-owned contributor and watcher membership in the authorized My Work system view
goal: Complete CAP-CMD-101 canonical My Work view membership for currently authorized Incident/Task owner, contributor and watcher relationships, consuming CAP-CMD-103 read-only operational ownership without changing assignment rights.
invariants: Canonical capability owner is CAP-CMD-101; CAP-CMD-103 owns Command operational membership source and any Class-2 mutation, not this read-only projection.
Git parent PR #172 frozen HEAD 705447943328c6edbeec95cb1a6b0a2760ebce64 is NOT engineering/business parent epic E10-CMD-101.

For MyWork, source Item.Owner OR source Contributors OR Watchers OR legacy Followers membership is a view predicate, never permission; host Owner.CanRead runs first per same-tenant/environment Incident/Task.
Only current host SessionScope.Principal matches exact source-provided member ID; no user-supplied principal/team scope or substring matches.
Do not rename owner, change relations, create a second membership provider, render raw member arrays or widen provider/source permissions.
Exactly six Command system views, existing GET route, filters, grouped/sorted 50-row pages, owner-revocation cursor and source freshness stay unchanged.
security_properties: Tenant/environment prefilter and independent per-object CanRead still apply before any membership-based view selection.
Member identities are source owned; they are not emitted to JSON, HTML, diagnostics or cursor payload; denied and foreign rows cannot affect public output.
Existing owner filter compares actual Item.Owner, never contributor/watch membership; revocation reprojects the queue on subsequent request.

migration.rationale: Backward compatible opt-in optional source-owned membership fields; legacy Followers and all serialized Row/Result forms remain unchanged.

rollback.strategy: Remove new contributor/watcher Item fields and matching branches; keep existing Followers/owner behavior.
verification: Historical six views, filters, group/sort/cursor and host-authorization tests still pass.

inputs: Canonical CAP-CMD-101 §§1-27, exact six Saved View keys (my-work = owner/contributor/watcher), CAP-CMD-103 §§1-27, Incident/Task objects and tenant/permission contracts.
Parent PR #172 grouping SHA 705447943328c6edbeec95cb1a6b0a2760ebce64 DRAFT, exact-head command-work-queue-runtime and engineering-kernel COMPLETED SUCCESS.
Current Work Queue Item has only Owner and legacy Followers, so independently supplied contributor/watcher roles are not represented or projected.
outputs: Existing first-party MyWork view now displays owner-authorized readable Incidents and Tasks matching source-owned primary Owner, Contributor, Watcher or legacy Follower.
No extra source calls, routes, ACLs, byte copies of relations or permissions; existing source-owner predicate remains authoritative.
Tests prove roles, foreign/denied/revoked absence, exact owner-only filter still respects actual responsible Owner and no raw membership disclosure.
acceptance_tests: Authorized sole contributor and sole watcher objects appear in MyWork alongside existing Owner and legacy Follower; denied same-tenant and foreign Watcher/Contributor are absent, with no foreign ACL lookup.
OwnerFilter=analyst selects only objects with actual owner analyst, not merely contributor/watch status; no membership metadata is exported.
Second authenticated request after owner.CanRead revocation hides prior watcher, and invalid client principal query fails on same canonical route.
Exact-head Go Linux/macOS/Windows and engineering-kernel mandated coverage (changed-security floor >=90), SAST, manifests/complexity/architecture/deps PASS; no merge unless upstream approved.

performance_budget.rationale: Membership scan is only over bounded existing host-provided lists of already owner-authorized same-scope candidates; no extra provider/network calls and unchanged 5000/50 item limits.
metrics: No additional Owner.List or Owner.CanRead calls compared to existing MyWork.
No new sort/page traversal or external membership lookup.
